name: Bvlgari Hotel Roma
positioning: Bvlgari's hotel in Rome's Campo Marzio district, on Piazza Augusto Imperatore, with a spa styled after ancient Roman baths
best_for: Travelers who want a central Rome base with a spa
Food and cocktail lovers drawn to a Niko Romito restaurant and the Bvlgari Bar

facts.text: The hotel is at Piazza Augusto Imperatore in the Campo Marzio district of Rome.
The building was renovated by the architecture firm ACPV (Antonio Citterio Patricia Viel).
Il Ristorante - Niko Romito is on the fifth floor and has a view over the Mausoleum of Augustus.
Chef Niko Romito's menu reinvents contemporary Italian cuisine in a concept developed exclusively for Bvlgari Hotels & Resorts.
The Bvlgari Bar has an outside bar and two terraces, one onto Via di Ripetta and one onto Piazza Augusto Imperatore.
Il Caffè, on the ground floor, was the first cafe created by Niko Romito.
The rooms are divided into four colour palettes: white, yellow, red and green.
The spa treatments are designed by Augustinus Bader.
The hotel has a library dedicated to the history of jewellery.
The Magnificent Path, an exclusive walking tour of Rome, begins at the hotel.

highlights.text: The Bvlgari Bar has a black marble bar top finished with 110 Murano glass twirls hand blown with gold dust by Barovier&Toso.
The Bvlgari Suite looks out over the Mausoleum of Emperor Augustus.
The Bvlgari Spa evokes ancient Roman baths, with marble columns rising from the swimming pool.
The private dining room has walls upholstered in Rubelli fabric depicting the twelve signs of the Zodiac.
The spa has a Spa Suite with a green onyx bath.

considerations.text: The Lobby Lounge is reserved for hotel guests throughout the day.
WhataHotel notes an ultra-luxury pricing point.
WhataHotel notes limited availability because of the hotel's exclusive size.
